arxiv-2109-02593.title: General-Purpose Question-Answering with Macaw
arxiv-2109-02593.creator: Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark
arxiv-2109-02593.description: Abstract Despite the successes of pretrained language models, there are still few high-quality, general-purpose QA systems that are freely available. In response, we present Macaw , a versatile, generative question-answering (QA) system that we are making available to the community.

arxiv-2110-01709.title: Benchmarking Memory-Centric Computing Systems: Analysis of Real Processing-in-Memory Hardware
arxiv-2110-01709.creator: Juan Gómez-Luna, Izzat El Hajj, Ivan Fernandez, Christina Giannoula, Geraldo F. Oliveira, Onur Mutlu
arxiv-2110-01709.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Juan Gómez-Luna, Izzat El Hajj, Ivan Fernandez, Christina Giannoula, Geraldo F. Oliveira, Onur Mutlu. Many modern workloads such as neural network inference and graph processing are fundamentally memory-bound. For such workloads, data movement between memory and CPU cores imposes a significant overhead in terms of both latency and energy. A major reason is that this communication happens through a narrow bus with high latency and limited bandwidth, and the low data reuse in memory-bound workloads is insufficient to amortize the cost of memory access.

arxiv-2205-03214.title: Modularized Bilinear Koopman Operator for Modeling and Predicting Transients of Microgrids
arxiv-2205-03214.creator: Xinyuan Jiang, Yan Li, Daning Huang
arxiv-2205-03214.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xinyuan Jiang, Yan Li, Daning Huang. Modularized Koopman Bilinear Form (M-KBF) is presented to model and predict the transient dynamics of microgrids in the presence of disturbances. As a scalable data-driven approach, M-KBF divides the identification and prediction of the high-dimensional nonlinear system into the individual study of subsystems; and thus, alleviating the difficulty of intensively handling high volume data and overcoming the curse of dimensionality.

arxiv-2303-09905.title: More Robust Schema-Guided Dialogue State Tracking via Tree-Based Paraphrase Ranking
arxiv-2303-09905.creator: Alexandru Coca, Bo-Hsiang Tseng, Weizhe Lin, Bill Byrne
arxiv-2303-09905.description: Abstract The schema-guided paradigm overcomes scalability issues inherent in building task-oriented dialogue (TOD) agents with static ontologies. Instead of operating on dialogue context alone, agents have access to hierarchical schemas containing task-relevant natural language descriptions. Fine-tuned language models excel at schema-guided dialogue state tracking (DST) but are sensitive to the writing style of the schemas.

arxiv-2304-10650.title: Learning a quantum computer’s capability
arxiv-2304-10650.creator: DANIEL HOTHEM 1, KEVIN YOUNG 1, TOMMIE CATANACH 2, TIMOTHY PROCTOR. 1
arxiv-2304-10650.description: Abstract Accurately predicting a quantum computer’s capability—which circuits it can run and how well it can run them—is a foundational goal of quantum characterization and benchmarking. As modern quantum computers become increasingly hard to simulate, we must develop accurate and scalable predictive capability models to help researchers and stakeholders decide which quantum computers to build and use.

arxiv-2306-09672.title: A Generalized vanishing theorem for Blow-ups of Quasi-smooth Stacks
arxiv-2306-09672.creator: Yu Zhao
arxiv-2306-09672.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhao. We prove a generalized vanishing theorem for certain quasi-coherent sheaves along the derived blow-ups of quasi-smooth derived Artin stacks. We give four applications of the generalized vanishing theorem: we prove a K K -theoretic version of the generalized vanishing theorem which verified a conjecture of the author [ 31 ] and give a new proof of the K K -theoretic localization theorem for quasi-smooth derived schemes through the intrinsic blow-up theory of Kiem-Li-Savvas [ 17 ] ; we prove a desingularization theorem

arxiv-2306-17086.title: NANOGrav Signal from a Dark Conformal Phase Transition
arxiv-2306-17086.creator: Kohei Fujikura 1 , Sudhakantha Girmohanta 2,3 , Yuichiro Nakai 2,3 and Motoo Suzuki 4,5 1 Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, University of Tokyo, Komaba, Meguro-ku, Tokyo 153-8902, Japan 2 Tsung-Dao Lee Institute, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, 520 Shengrong Road, Shanghai 201210, China 3 School
arxiv-2306-17086.description: Abstract We explore the possibility that a confining first-order phase transition of a nearly-conformal dark sector generates the reported NANOGrav signal of a stochastic gravitational wave background. The visible Standard Model (SM) sector and the dark sector are initially thermally decoupled so that their temperatures are different.

arxiv-2503-21831.title: Thermodynamics of the XX spin chain in the QTM approach
arxiv-2503-21831.creator: P. N. Bibikov
arxiv-2503-21831.description: Abstract The free energy density of the XX chain in a magnetic field is obtained in two alternative ways within the Quantum Transfer Matrix approach. In both cases the calculations are complete and self-consistent. All the intermediate constructions are presented explicitly in detail.

pmc-10580130.title: The Vinyasa Tool for mHealth Solutions: Supporting Human-Centered Design in Nascent Digital Health Ecosystems
pmc-10580130.creator: Verghese Thomas, Bharat Kalidindi, Abijeet Waghmare, Abhishek Bhatia, Tony Raj, Satchit Balsari
pmc-10580130.description: BackgroundmHealth (mobile health) systems have been deployed widely in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) for health system strengthening, requiring considerable resource allocation. However, most solutions have not achieved scale or sustainability. Poor usability and failure to address perceived needs are among the principal reasons mHealth systems fail to achieve acceptance and adoption by health care workers.

pmc-11430100.title: Prevalence of schistosomiasis and its association with anemia in Ethiopia, 2024: a systematic review and meta‑analysis
pmc-11430100.creator: Deresse Abebe Gebrehana, Gebretsadik Endeshaw Molla, Woretaw Endalew, Destaw Fetene Teshome, Fantahun Ayenew Mekonnen, Dessie Abebaw Angaw
pmc-11430100.description: BackgroundSchistosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease that affects over 250 million people, predominantly in impoverished communities, including those in Ethiopia. However, there is currently no available national data regarding its prevalence in Ethiopia or its potential association with anemia.MethodsThe Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA-2020) guideline was followed in our study.

pmc-11567114.title: Integrating near-infrared hyperspectral imaging with machine learning and feature selection: Detecting adulteration of extra-virgin olive oil with lower-grade olive oils and hazelnut oil
pmc-11567114.creator: Derick Malavi, Katleen Raes, Sam Van Haute
pmc-11567114.description: Detecting adulteration in extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) is particularly challenging with oils of similar chemical composition. This study applies near-infrared hyperspectral imaging (NIR-HSI) and machine learning (ML) to detect EVOO adulteration with hazelnut, refined olive, and olive pomace oils at various concentrations (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%, and 100% m/m).

pmc-12419670.title: Do chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) attribute preferences to virtual competitors?
pmc-12419670.creator: Emilie Rapport Munro, Matthias Allritz, Kenneth Schweller, Daniel B. M. Haun, Josep Call, James Brereton, James Brereton, James Brereton
pmc-12419670.description: Many animal species live in multi-level societies regulated by complex patterns of dominance. Avoiding competition with dominant group-mates for resources such as food and mates is an important skill for subordinate individuals in these societies, if they wish to evade harassment and aggression. Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) are an example of such a species.

pmc-12524750.title: Systematic Review of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Adult Sickle Cell Disease
pmc-12524750.creator: Safa Khalil Ebrahim Al Taitoon, Kannan Sridharan, Davide Alberto Chiumello, Jesús Villar
pmc-12524750.description: Background: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a hereditary hemoglobinopathy associated with life-threatening complications such as acute chest syndrome (ACS), which may necessitate extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in refractory cases. Despite growing use, ECMO in SCD remains challenging due to risks of hemolysis, thrombosis, and anticoagulation complications.

pmc-12530034.description: The addition of a small amount of silicon to the anode material is a widely used approach to increase the energy density of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, its (de‐)lithiation leads to volume changes, resulting in structural degradation and the formation of an insufficient solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI), limiting the cycle life and electrochemical performance.

pmc-12563728.title: Prevalence of Traumatic Dental Injuries to Anterior Teeth among 14- to 60-year-Old Patients in Mysuru, India: A Hospital-Based Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12563728.creator: Paras M. Gehlot, Annapoorna B. Mariswamy, Nandlal Bhojraj, L Krishna Prasad
pmc-12563728.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objective:Traumatic dental injuries (TDIs) are a major public health concern, particularly affecting anterior teeth due to their prominent position. While global prevalence ranges from 6 to 59%, limited epidemiological data exist for Mysuru district, Karnataka, India.

pmc-12994586.title: Anti-inflammatory potential of plant-derived extracellular vesicles from Solanum nigrum L. integrated in gelatine-dopamine hydrogel on RAW 264.7 and MC3T3 cells
pmc-12994586.creator: Anggraini Barlian, Tasya Fediarisa, Aida Fitri Kamila, Noviana Vanawati, Yung-Hsin Cheng
pmc-12994586.description: Background and purposePlant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEV) from Solanum nigrum L. fruit show promise as a cell-free regenerative and inflammatory therapy for bone defects due to their anti-inflammatory properties. However, challenges such as storage stability and targeted delivery efficiency remain in PDEV's applications. Strategies such as lyophilization and injectable hydrogel delivery systems offer potential solutions.

pmc-13173944.title: Widespread ST segment elevation and elevated troponin: unveiling an uncommon cause
pmc-13173944.creator: Fei Wang, Ziyi Sun
pmc-13173944.description: This article describes a case involving a patient who presented with chest pain persisting for three days, elevated levels of cardiac troponin, and widespread ST segment elevation in the ECG leads. Subsequent diagnosis revealed esophageal perforation resulting from the accidental ingestion of a fish bone, leading to pericardial effusion and pneumopericardium.

pmc-13574273.title: Sevelamer carbonate crystal associated colitis in a hemodialysis patient: a case report
pmc-13574273.creator: Omair Bseiso, Ma’moun Qawasmeh, Anas Zahdeh, Obay Isayed, Abrar Omari, Motaz Natsheh
pmc-13574273.description: Sevelamer carbonate, a non-calcium phosphate binder widely used in end-stage renal disease (ESRD), is an increasingly recognized but underdiagnosed cause of medication-induced colitis through gastrointestinal crystal deposition. We report a 56-year-old Palestinian male with ESRD on hemodialysis who presented with a one-month history of watery non-bloody diarrhea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal pain.

pmc-7619564.title: PIEZO1 force sensing in cardiac electrical modelling
pmc-7619564.creator: Yurou Cai, Michael A Colman, David J Beech
pmc-7619564.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). also highly mechanical. They rightly address the challenge by focusing on the PIEZO1 channel. While not the only force sensor in the heart, PIEZO1 is an especially well defined force sensor at protein structural and functional levels and widely accepted by investigators as dedicated to mechanical force sensing (Xiao, 2024).
